images.title: Compass opened to 4 cm
images.purpose: Show that the opening of a compass is the distance from P to every spot it draws.
images.composition: A compass standing on P in the centre of a drawn circle, wide margins.
images.exact_structure: One compass with legs opened so that tip and pencil are exactly 4 cm apart, tip on spot P (amber #E69F00 dot). One teal #0072B2 circle of radius 4 cm drawn around P. One straight reddish purple #CC79A7 line from P to the circle, labelled 4 cm. Exactly 1 compass, 1 circle, 1 line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a compass opening other than 4 cm
images.takeaway: The compass opening is the distance from P to every spot.
images.description: A compass opened to 4 cm with its tip on P, a teal circle of radius 4 cm around P and a purple line from P to the circle labelled 4 cm.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the opening of the compass and say what it equals.

image_decisions.why: Showing the opening equal to the radius is one clear picture.
